value: This U.S. industry comprises establishments primarily engaged in one of the following: (1) growing crops (except oilseeds and/or grains; vegetables and/or melons; fruits and/or tree nuts; greenhouse, nursery, and/or floriculture products; tobacco; cotton; sugarcane; hay; sugar beets; or peanuts); (2) growing a combination of crops (except a combination of oilseed(s) and grain(s); and a combination of fruit(s) and tree nut(s)) with no one crop or family of crops accounting for one-half of the establishment's agricultural production (i.e., value of crops for market); or (3) gathering tea or maple sap.
Cannabis, grown in an open field
General combination crop farming (except fruit and nut combinations, oilseed and grain, vegetable)
Hemp, grown in an open field
Maple sap concentrating (i.e., producing pure maple syrup in the field)
Marijuana, grown in an open field
Syrup, pure maple (i.e., maple syrup reducing)
